pictures.scene: Peter Paul Rubens, King David Playing the Harp — the old king seen close from behind and a little to the side, his white hair and long grey beard lit against the dark and his face lifted away from us, a heavy white fur mantle over a gold robe with a jewelled chain laid twice across his shoulders, and both hands in among the strings of the harp standing up in front of him, for the choirmaster with stringed instruments, a Psalm of David
pictures.name: pd_rubens_king_david_harp

pictures.scene: Giovanni Bellini, The Agony in the Garden — Christ kneeling up on the bare rise in a blue mantle over a red robe, barefoot, His face turned up and both hands lifted open before Him, the dawn coming pink along the hills behind, two disciples fallen asleep on the ground below Him, and the file of armed men already winding along the road in the middle distance, answer me when I call O God of my righteousness, You have relieved my distress
pictures.name: pd_bellini_gebed_in_de_hof_van_olijven

pictures.scene: Gerard van Honthorst, Christ before the High Priest — the one candle standing on the table between them in the dark room, the old priest leaning over his open book with his finger up in the air making his charge, and Christ standing opposite in a plain white robe with His hands quietly folded in front of Him, saying nothing, the soldiers and the bystanders watching out of the shadows behind, show me grace and hear my prayer, how long O men will my honor be maligned
pictures.name: pd_honthorst_christ_before_the_high_priest

pictures.scene: Abraham van Beyeren, Sumptuous Still Life — the rich table loaded in the half dark, a tall covered gold cup and a glass of rose wine standing up at the back, bunches of pale and black grapes with a peach and an orange heaped at the side, a silver bowl and a knife with a worked handle and a boxwood flute laid across the front, a lobster claw and a gold watch left lying among it, and the white cloth slipping off the edge of the table toward us, how long will you love vanity and seek after lies
pictures.name: pd_van_beyeren_sumptuous_still_life

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, An Elderly Man in Prayer — the old man close up out of the brown dark, his grey hair and long white beard catching the light and his eyes shut, his two worn hands laid palm to palm in front of his face, a plain coarse robe on his shoulders and the big book lying open under his elbows, know that the LORD has set apart the godly for Himself, the LORD hears when I call to Him
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_elderly_man_in_prayer

pictures.scene: Francisco de Zurbaran, Saint Francis in Meditation — the friar kneeling alone against a bare grey wall in a patched brown habit with the knotted cord hanging down from his waist, the deep hood pulled forward so that only his open mouth and his beard come out of the shadow, his face turned up and his two hands holding a skull against his breast, be angry yet do not sin, on your bed search your heart and be still
pictures.name: pd_zurbaran_saint_francis_in_meditation

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Sacrifice of Manoah — the old man and his wife kneeling together on the ground in the firelight, he bent right over with his white beard down on his chest and his hands clasped hard in front of his face, she upright beside him in a red mantle and a white head cloth with her palms laid together and her eyes closed, the whole dark room glowing behind them, offer the sacrifices of the righteous and trust in the LORD
pictures.name: pd_the_sacrifice_of_manoah

pictures.scene: William Holman Hunt, The Light of the World — Christ standing at night in the weeds and the fallen apples outside a door nobody has opened in years, a white robe under a jewelled clasp and a heavy red mantle, the crown of thorns on His head with a faint gold ring of light behind it, one hand lifted to knock and the other holding down a pierced lantern whose candle throws the only light there is, many ask who can show us the good, shine the light of Your face upon us O LORD
pictures.name: pd_hunt_the_light_of_the_world

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Harvesters — the standing wheat cut back in a wide swathe with the sheaves stood up in stooks across the stubble, reapers still bent at work out in the field and the church tower showing over the trees behind, and in front the whole crew sitting down under the pear tree to eat, one tipping up a jug, the women spooning from their bowls, the bread and the knife out on a white cloth, and one man flat on his back asleep against the trunk, You have filled my heart with more joy than when grain and new wine abound
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_harvesters

pictures.scene: Aert de Gelder, Jacob's Dream — the whole hillside left in brown dark with one bare thorn tree on it, Jacob lying stretched out asleep on the bare ground at the bottom with his head on the stone, and up in the air above him the light breaking open and the angels coming down out of it with their wings spread, one close and one far up in the glare, in peace I will lie down and sleep, for You alone O LORD make me dwell in safety
pictures.name: pd_de_gelder_jacobs_dream

lines.text: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments.
A Psalm of David.
Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness.
You have relieved my distress;
show me grace and hear my prayer.
How long, O men, will my honor be maligned?
How long will you love vanity
and seek after lies?
Know that the LORD has set apart the godly for Himself;
the LORD hears when I call to Him.
Be angry, yet do not sin;
on your bed, search your heart and be still.
Offer the sacrifices of the righteous
and trust in the LORD.
Many ask, Who can show us the good?
Shine the light of Your face upon us, O LORD.
You have filled my heart with more joy
than when grain and new wine abound.
In peace I will lie down and sleep,
for You alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety.
